1.7 Workflow: camera-card ingest with Photo Mechanic Plus

This is the workflow diskproxy was first written for. The PMP guide is the complete reference.

1.7.1 The problem

Photo Mechanic Plus records each ingested file’s path, size and modification time, and its incremental ingest copies only files it has not seen. On the exFAT cards examined, the camera wrote modification times without a valid timezone offset, so macOS interpreted them in whatever timezone the Mac was in when the card was mounted. After travelling, the same photo had a different modification time, Photo Mechanic thought it was new, and it copied the whole card again.

1.7.2 The fix

The pmp plugin presents the card as a virtual disk with a fixed timestamp convention. For a new card the convention is UTC; a card with existing history keeps the convention its history was made in, for example Pacific time. The plugin works out the offset the card was mounted in from up to three sampled photos, recorded in a small profile on the card when it is registered. The photos themselves, and their EXIF capture times, are never changed.

1.7.3 Setting up

scripts/install.sh --config configs/pmp.json

The example config expects the card at /Volumes/LEICA M; edit source for another card name, or pass the path to start.

1.7.4 Registering a new card

Finish any EXIF corrections first, then, with the card mounted in the timezone the Mac is currently set to:

diskproxy-server

With no command, diskproxy-server registers the card: it writes .pmingest.dat if it is absent and the profile .pmp-ingest-proxy.json to the card, and exits. If you run diskproxy start on an unregistered card, it simply prints Run diskproxy-server. If the Mac’s timezone changed while the card stayed mounted, remount it first, or give the offset it was mounted in:

diskproxy-server --source-offset=+09:00

Running the command again on a registered card reuses its profile unchanged. --register deliberately refreshes the samples after reviewed edits.

1.7.5 Ingesting

diskproxy start
# In Photo Mechanic Plus, ingest from the PMP Pacific volume under Disks.
diskproxy stop

Then eject the card. The volume is called PMP Pacific for compatibility, even for UTC cards; the label does not set the convention.

To hide photos already ingested, rather than relying on Photo Mechanic’s incremental history:

diskproxy start --set plugins.pmp.hide_ingested=true

The history is read once at start, so restart the view to hide newly ingested files.
